exposure: Underweight with gestational weight gain below, within, and above optimal range
Obese with gestational weight gain below, within, and above optimal range
Overweight with gestational weight gain below, within, and above optimal range
Normal weight with gestational weight gain below, within, and above optimal range
cohort: 97,157 women with singleton pregnancies registered in the Japan Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology (JSOG) Successive Pregnancy Birth Registry System between January 2013 and December 2013
finding: Higher pre-pregnancy BMI was associated with a higher incidence of pregnancy complications like gestational diabetes and cesarean delivery, while lower pre-pregnancy BMI was associated with a higher incidence of small for gestational age.
mod_finding: Higher pre-pregnancy BMI was associated with a higher incidence of cesarean delivery.
